Fake News Detection Using Machine Learning¶

Machine Learning I | University of Chicago, MS Applied Data Science

Section 0 — Setup & Imports¶

All core libraries are imported here. Optional packages (XGBoost, LightGBM, WordCloud, textstat, UMAP) are loaded with graceful fallbacks so the notebook runs in any environment.

Section 1 — Configuration & Global Settings¶

Central configuration block. Modify these parameters to control the notebook.

Parameter Default Description
SAMPLE_SIZE 25000 Stratified sample size. Set to None for full 72k (slower).
RANDOM_STATE 42 Random seed for reproducibility.
N_TOPICS 12 Number of topics for LDA / NMF / LSA.
N_CLUSTERS 2 Number of clusters for KMeans / GMM.

RANDOM_STATE = 42
N_TOPICS     = 12

Section 2 — Data Loading & Initial Exploration¶

The WELFake Dataset¶

WELFake (Well-balanced Fake news dataset) is a benchmark corpus of 72,134 news articles with balanced labels. It merges four widely used fake news datasets.

In [4]:
df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)
print(f"Raw shape: {df.shape}")
print(df.head(3).to_string())
print(f"\nDtypes:\n{df.dtypes}")
print(f"\nNulls:\n{df.isnull().sum()}")

df.columns = [c.strip().lower().replace(" ", "_") for c in df.columns]
# Drop index col if present
for c in df.columns:
    if "unnamed" in c:
        df.drop(columns=[c], inplace=True)

df["title"]  = df["title"].fillna("")
df["text"]   = df["text"].fillna("")
df["content"] = df["title"] + " " + df["text"]
df = df[df["content"].str.strip().str.len() > 30].reset_index(drop=True)

# Stratified sample
if SAMPLE_SIZE and len(df) > SAMPLE_SIZE:
    df = (df.groupby("label", group_keys=False)
            .apply(lambda x: x.sample(SAMPLE_SIZE // 2, random_state=RANDOM_STATE))
            .reset_index(drop=True))

print(f"\nWorking shape: {df.shape}")
print(f"Label balance:\n{df['label'].value_counts()}")

Section 3 — Text Preprocessing¶

We apply a standard NLP cleaning pipeline: lowercasing, contraction expansion, URL / mention normalization, lemmatization, and stopword removal.

In [5]:
CONTRACTIONS = {
    "won't": "will not", "can't": "cannot", "n't": " not",
    "'re": " are", "'ve": " have", "'ll": " will",
    "'d": " would", "'m": " am", "it's": "it is"
}

def expand_contractions(text):
    for k, v in CONTRACTIONS.items():
        text = text.replace(k, v)
    return text

def clean_text(text, lemmatize=True, remove_stops=True):
    text = str(text).lower()
    text = expand_contractions(text)
    text = re.sub(r"http\S+|www\S+", " URL ", text)
    text = re.sub(r"@\w+", " USER ", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\d+", " NUM ", text)
    text = re.sub(r"[^\w\s]", " ", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()
    tokens = text.split()
    if remove_stops:
        tokens = [t for t in tokens if t not in STOP_WORDS and len(t) > 2]
    if lemmatize:
        tokens = [LEMMATIZER.lemmatize(t) for t in tokens]
    return " ".join(tokens)

t0 = time.time()
df["clean"] = df["content"].apply(clean_text)
print(f"Done in {time.time()-t0:.1f}s")
print(df[["content","clean"]].head(2).to_string())

Section 4 — Feature Engineering¶

Beyond raw text, we engineer 19 handcrafted linguistic & stylistic features that capture writing style differences between fake and real news.

4.2 Lexical & Structural Features¶

In [6]:
def count_capitals(text):
    return sum(1 for c in text if c.isupper())

def exclamation_count(text):
    return text.count("!")

def question_count(text):
    return text.count("?")

def avg_word_len(text):
    words = text.split()
    return np.mean([len(w) for w in words]) if words else 0

def type_token_ratio(text):
    words = text.lower().split()
    return len(set(words)) / len(words) if words else 0

def count_quotes(text):
    return text.count('"') + text.count("'")

def has_url(text):
    return int(bool(re.search(r"http|www|\.com", text)))

def punct_ratio(text):
    return sum(1 for c in text if c in string.punctuation) / max(len(text), 1)

def sentence_count(text):
    return len(re.split(r"[.!?]+", text))

def avg_sentence_len(text):
    sents = [s.strip() for s in re.split(r"[.!?]+", text) if s.strip()]
    return np.mean([len(s.split()) for s in sents]) if sents else 0
In [7]:
df["word_count"]       = df["content"].str.split().str.len()
df["char_count"]       = df["content"].str.len()
df["unique_words"]     = df["content"].apply(lambda x: len(set(x.lower().split())))
df["cap_count"]        = df["content"].apply(count_capitals)
df["cap_ratio"]        = df["cap_count"] / df["char_count"].clip(lower=1)
df["exclamation"]      = df["content"].apply(exclamation_count)
df["question"]         = df["content"].apply(question_count)
df["avg_word_len"]     = df["content"].apply(avg_word_len)
df["ttr"]              = df["content"].apply(type_token_ratio)
df["quote_count"]      = df["content"].apply(count_quotes)
df["has_url"]          = df["content"].apply(has_url)
df["punct_ratio"]      = df["content"].apply(punct_ratio)
df["sentence_count"]   = df["content"].apply(sentence_count)
df["avg_sent_len"]     = df["content"].apply(avg_sentence_len)
df["title_word_count"] = df["title"].str.split().str.len().fillna(0)
df["title_cap_ratio"]  = df["title"].apply(count_capitals) / df["title"].str.len().clip(lower=1)

# Sentiment features using VADER
df["sent_neg"]      = df["content"].apply(lambda x: SIA.polarity_scores(x[:512])["neg"])
df["sent_neu"]      = df["content"].apply(lambda x: SIA.polarity_scores(x[:512])["neu"])
df["sent_pos"]      = df["content"].apply(lambda x: SIA.polarity_scores(x[:512])["pos"])
df["sent_compound"] = df["content"].apply(lambda x: SIA.polarity_scores(x[:512])["compound"])

4.4 Readability Features (textstat)¶

In [9]:
# Readability
if HAS_TS:
    df["flesch"]     = df["content"].apply(lambda x: textstat.flesch_reading_ease(x[:1000]))
    df["fk_grade"]   = df["content"].apply(lambda x: textstat.flesch_kincaid_grade(x[:1000]))
    df["smog"]       = df["content"].apply(lambda x: textstat.smog_index(x[:1000]))
    df["dale_chall"] = df["content"].apply(lambda x: textstat.dale_chall_readability_score(x[:1000]))

HANDCRAFTED = ["word_count","char_count","unique_words","cap_ratio","exclamation",
               "question","avg_word_len","ttr","quote_count","has_url","punct_ratio",
               "sentence_count","avg_sent_len","title_word_count","title_cap_ratio",
               "sent_neg","sent_neu","sent_pos","sent_compound"]
if HAS_TS:
    HANDCRAFTED += ["flesch","fk_grade","smog","dale_chall"]

print(f"Handcrafted features ({len(HANDCRAFTED)}):")
print(df.groupby("label")[HANDCRAFTED[:10]].mean().T.rename(columns={0:"Fake",1:"Real"}).to_string())

Section 5 — Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)¶

We explore how features and linguistic patterns differ between fake and real news articles.

5A — Feature Distributions by Class¶

In [10]:
feats_to_plot = ["word_count","cap_ratio","exclamation","ttr",
                 "sent_compound","avg_word_len","punct_ratio","avg_sent_len"]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(18, 7))
axes = axes.flatten()
for ax, feat in zip(axes, feats_to_plot):
    for label, name, color in zip([0,1],["Fake","Real"],[RED, BLUE]):
        data = df[df["label"]==label][feat].clip(
            df[feat].quantile(0.01), df[feat].quantile(0.99))
        ax.hist(data, bins=40, alpha=0.6, color=color, label=name, density=True)
    ax.set_title(feat); ax.legend(fontsize=8)
plt.suptitle("Feature Distributions by Class", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

5B — Correlation Heatmap¶

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 11))
mask = np.triu(np.ones_like(corr_df, dtype=bool))
sns.heatmap(corr_df, mask=mask, cmap="RdBu_r", center=0, annot=True,
            fmt=".2f", annot_kws={"size": 6}, ax=ax, linewidths=0.3)
ax.set_title("Feature Correlation Matrix (incl. label)", fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

5D — N-gram Frequency Analysis¶

In [13]:
def top_ngrams(corpus, n, top_k=20):
    vec = CountVectorizer(ngram_range=(n,n), stop_words="english",
                          max_features=100000).fit(corpus)
    bag = vec.transform(corpus)
    counts = np.asarray(bag.sum(axis=0)).flatten()
    return sorted(zip(vec.get_feature_names_out(), counts),
                  key=lambda x: -x[1])[:top_k]

fake_text = df[df["label"]==0]["clean"]
real_text = df[df["label"]==1]["clean"]

for n, label_n in [(1,"Unigrams"), (2,"Bigrams"), (3,"Trigrams")]:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 5))
    for ax, corpus, title, color in zip(axes,
                                        [fake_text, real_text],
                                        [f"FAKE — {label_n}", f"REAL — {label_n}"],
                                        [RED, BLUE]):
        grams = top_ngrams(corpus, n)
        words, cnts = zip(*grams)
        ax.barh(words[::-1], cnts[::-1], color=color, alpha=0.85)
        ax.set_title(title, fontweight="bold")
    plt.suptitle(f"Top 20 {label_n}", fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

5G — Part-of-Speech (POS) Tag Distribution¶

In [16]:
sample_df = df.sample(min(2000, len(df)), random_state=RANDOM_STATE)

def pos_counts(text):
    tokens = word_tokenize(text[:500])
    tags = pos_tag(tokens)
    counts = Counter(tag for _, tag in tags)
    return counts

pos_by_class = {0: Counter(), 1: Counter()}
for _, row in sample_df.iterrows():
    pos_by_class[row["label"]].update(pos_counts(row["content"]))

common_tags = ["NN","NNS","NNP","NNPS","VB","VBD","VBZ","JJ","RB","IN","DT","PRP","CC"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, 5))
x = np.arange(len(common_tags))
w = 0.35
total0 = sum(pos_by_class[0].values())
total1 = sum(pos_by_class[1].values())
ax.bar(x - w/2, [pos_by_class[0][t]/total0 for t in common_tags], w,
       color=RED, alpha=0.85, label="Fake")
ax.bar(x + w/2, [pos_by_class[1][t]/total1 for t in common_tags], w,
       color=BLUE, alpha=0.85, label="Real")
ax.set_xticks(x); ax.set_xticklabels(common_tags)
ax.set_ylabel("Proportion"); ax.set_title("POS Tag Distribution", fontweight="bold")
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Section 6 — Vectorization¶

We convert text to numerical feature matrices using several complementary techniques.

In [17]:
X_raw = df["content"]
X_clean = df["clean"]
y = df["label"].values

X_train_raw, X_test_raw, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X_raw, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=RANDOM_STATE, stratify=y)
X_train_clean, X_test_clean = (X_clean.loc[X_train_raw.index],
                                X_clean.loc[X_test_raw.index])

6.1 TF-IDF Word Unigrams + Bigrams¶

In [18]:
tfidf_word = TfidfVectorizer(max_features=60000, ngram_range=(1,2),
                              sublinear_tf=True, min_df=3,
                              stop_words="english", analyzer="word")
Xtr_tfidf = tfidf_word.fit_transform(X_train_clean)
Xte_tfidf = tfidf_word.transform(X_test_clean)
print(f"Shape: {Xtr_tfidf.shape}")

Shape: (20000, 60000)

6.2 TF-IDF Character N-grams¶

In [19]:
tfidf_char = TfidfVectorizer(max_features=40000, ngram_range=(3,5),
                              sublinear_tf=True, min_df=5,
                              analyzer="char_wb")
Xtr_char = tfidf_char.fit_transform(X_train_clean)
Xte_char = tfidf_char.transform(X_test_clean)
print(f"Shape: {Xtr_char.shape}")

Shape: (20000, 40000)

6.3 Bag-of-Words¶

In [20]:
bow = CountVectorizer(max_features=50000, ngram_range=(1,2),
                      stop_words="english", min_df=3)
Xtr_bow = bow.fit_transform(X_train_clean)
Xte_bow  = bow.transform(X_test_clean)
print(f"Shape: {Xtr_bow.shape}")

Shape: (20000, 50000)

6.4 Hashing Vectorizer¶

In [21]:
hashing = HashingVectorizer(n_features=2**17, ngram_range=(1,2),
                             stop_words="english", norm="l2")
Xtr_hash = hashing.transform(X_train_clean)
Xte_hash  = hashing.transform(X_test_clean)
print(f"Shape: {Xtr_hash.shape}")

Shape: (20000, 131072)

6.5 Combined Feature Matrix (TF-IDF word + char + handcrafted)¶

In [22]:
from scipy.sparse import csr_matrix, hstack as sp_hstack
scaler = StandardScaler()
train_idx = X_train_raw.index
test_idx  = X_test_raw.index
Xtr_hc = csr_matrix(scaler.fit_transform(df.loc[train_idx, HANDCRAFTED].fillna(0)))
Xte_hc = csr_matrix(scaler.transform(df.loc[test_idx,  HANDCRAFTED].fillna(0)))

# Combined: TF-IDF word + char + handcrafted
Xtr_combo = sp_hstack([Xtr_tfidf, Xtr_char, Xtr_hc])
Xte_combo = sp_hstack([Xte_tfidf, Xte_char, Xte_hc])
print(f"Combined shape: {Xtr_combo.shape}")

Combined shape: (20000, 100019)

6.6 Feature Selection — Mutual Information & Chi-Squared¶

In [23]:
print("\nTop 20 TF-IDF features by Mutual Information:")

feat_names = np.array(tfidf_word.get_feature_names_out())
top20_mi = feat_names[np.argsort(mi)[-20:][::-1]]
print("  ", list(top20_mi))

top20_chi2 = feat_names[np.argsort(chi2_scores)[-20:][::-1]]
print("  ", list(top20_chi2))

Section 7 — Supervised Learning & Model Comparison¶

We train and evaluate 14 supervised classifiers spanning linear models, naive Bayes, tree ensembles, and gradient boosting methods.

In [24]:
from sklearn.decomposition import TruncatedSVD
_svd_trees = TruncatedSVD(n_components=50, random_state=RANDOM_STATE)
Xtr_svd_trees = _svd_trees.fit_transform(Xtr_tfidf)
Xte_svd_trees = _svd_trees.transform(Xte_tfidf)
print(f"SVD-50 for tree models: {Xtr_svd_trees.shape}")

MODELS = {
    "Logistic Regression":       LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, C=5.0,
                                                    solver="saga", n_jobs=-1,
                                                    random_state=RANDOM_STATE),
    "Ridge Classifier":          RidgeClassifier(alpha=1.0),
    "SGD (hinge/SVM)":           SGDClassifier(loss="hinge", max_iter=1000,
                                               tol=1e-3, n_jobs=-1,
                                               random_state=RANDOM_STATE),
    "SGD (log/LR)":              SGDClassifier(loss="modified_huber", max_iter=1000,
                                               n_jobs=-1, random_state=RANDOM_STATE),
    "Linear SVC":                CalibratedClassifierCV(
                                     LinearSVC(max_iter=3000,
                                               random_state=RANDOM_STATE), cv=3),
    "Naive Bayes (Multinomial)": MultinomialNB(alpha=0.05),
    "Naive Bayes (Complement)":  ComplementNB(alpha=0.05),
    "Naive Bayes (Bernoulli)":   BernoulliNB(alpha=0.05),
    "Decision Tree":             DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=20,
                                                        min_samples_leaf=10,
                                                        random_state=RANDOM_STATE),
    "Extra Trees":               ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=100,
                                                      max_features="sqrt",
                                                      n_jobs=-1,
                                                      random_state=RANDOM_STATE),
    "Random Forest":             RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100,
                                                        max_features="sqrt",
                                                        n_jobs=-1,
                                                        random_state=RANDOM_STATE),

                                     max_iter=200, max_depth=5,
                                     learning_rate=0.1,

}

if HAS_XGB:
    MODELS["XGBoost"] = xgb.XGBClassifier(
        n_estimators=200, max_depth=5, learning_rate=0.1,
        eval_metric="logloss", random_state=RANDOM_STATE, n_jobs=-1)
if HAS_LGB:
    MODELS["LightGBM"] = lgb.LGBMClassifier(
        n_estimators=200, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.1,
        random_state=RANDOM_STATE, n_jobs=-1, verbose=-1)

SPARSE_MODELS = {"Naive Bayes (Multinomial)", "Naive Bayes (Complement)",
                 "Naive Bayes (Bernoulli)"}
TREE_MODELS   = {"Decision Tree", "Extra Trees", "Random Forest",
                 "Hist Gradient Boosting", "XGBoost", "LightGBM"}

results = {}
print(f"\n{'Model':<38} {'Acc':>7} {'F1':>7} {'Prec':>7} {'Rec':>7} {'Time':>8}")
print("─" * 75)

for name, clf in MODELS.items():
    t0 = time.time()
    if name in SPARSE_MODELS:
        Xtr, Xte = Xtr_tfidf, Xte_tfidf
    elif name in TREE_MODELS:
        Xtr, Xte = Xtr_svd_trees, Xte_svd_trees
    else:
        Xtr, Xte = Xtr_combo, Xte_combo
    try:
        clf.fit(Xtr, y_train)
        preds = clf.predict(Xte)
        rep   = classification_report(y_test, preds, output_dict=True, zero_division=0)
        elapsed = time.time() - t0
        results[name] = {
            "accuracy":  rep["accuracy"],
            "f1":        rep["weighted avg"]["f1-score"],
            "precision": rep["weighted avg"]["precision"],
            "recall":    rep["weighted avg"]["recall"],
            "time_s":    elapsed,
            "preds":     preds,
            "clf":       clf,
            "Xte":       Xte,
            "Xtr":       Xtr,
        }
        print(f"{name:<38} {rep['accuracy']:>7.4f} {rep['weighted avg']['f1-score']:>7.4f} "
              f"{rep['weighted avg']['precision']:>7.4f} {rep['weighted avg']['recall']:>7.4f} "
              f"{elapsed:>7.1f}s")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"{name:<38} ERROR: {e}")

7.2 Voting Ensemble (Top-3 Classifiers)¶

In [26]:
top3_names = sorted(results, key=lambda k: results[k]["f1"], reverse=True)[:5]
estimators = []
for n in top3_names:
    clf = results[n]["clf"]
    if hasattr(clf, "predict_proba"):
        estimators.append((n[:15], clf))
        if len(estimators) == 3:
            break
if len(estimators) >= 2:
    voting_clf = VotingClassifier(estimators=estimators, voting="soft", n_jobs=-1)
    voting_clf.fit(Xtr_combo, y_train)
    voting_preds = voting_clf.predict(Xte_combo)
    vrep = classification_report(y_test, voting_preds, output_dict=True, zero_division=0)
    print(f"Voting Ensemble — Acc: {vrep['accuracy']:.4f}  F1: {vrep['weighted avg']['f1-score']:.4f}")
    results["Voting Ensemble"] = {
        "accuracy":  vrep["accuracy"],
        "f1":        vrep["weighted avg"]["f1-score"],
        "precision": vrep["weighted avg"]["precision"],
        "recall":    vrep["weighted avg"]["recall"],
        "preds":     voting_preds,
        "clf":       voting_clf,
        "Xte":       Xte_combo,
        "Xtr":       Xtr_combo,
    }

7.4 Performance Comparison & ROC Curves¶

In [28]:
res_df = pd.DataFrame({k: {m: results[k][m] for m in ["accuracy","f1","precision","recall"]}
                        for k in results}).T.sort_values("f1", ascending=False)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(18, 6))

# Bar chart
x = np.arange(len(res_df))
w = 0.2
palette = ["#2196F3","#4CAF50","#FF9800","#F44336"]
for i, (metric, color) in enumerate(zip(["accuracy","f1","precision","recall"], palette)):
    axes[0].bar(x + i*w, res_df[metric], w, label=metric.capitalize(), color=color, alpha=0.85)
axes[0].set_xticks(x + w*1.5)
axes[0].set_xticklabels(res_df.index, rotation=35, ha="right", fontsize=8)
axes[0].set_ylim(0.8, 1.02)
axes[0].set_title("All Models — Performance Comparison", fontweight="bold")
axes[0].legend()

# ROC curves
for name, res in results.items():
    clf_r = res["clf"]
    Xte_cur = res["Xte"]
    try:
        if hasattr(clf_r, "predict_proba"):
            proba = clf_r.predict_proba(Xte_cur)[:,1]
        elif hasattr(clf_r, "decision_function"):
            proba = clf_r.decision_function(Xte_cur)
        else:
            continue
        fpr, tpr, _ = roc_curve(y_test, proba)
        roc_auc = auc(fpr, tpr)
        axes[1].plot(fpr, tpr, label=f"{name[:20]} ({roc_auc:.3f})", linewidth=1.2)
    except:
        pass
axes[1].plot([0,1],[0,1],"k--", lw=0.8)
axes[1].set_xlabel("FPR"); axes[1].set_ylabel("TPR")
axes[1].set_title("ROC Curves", fontweight="bold")
axes[1].legend(fontsize=7, loc="lower right")
plt.suptitle("Supervised Model Evaluation", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

7.5 Confusion Matrices — Top 4 Models¶

In [29]:
top4 = res_df.head(4).index.tolist()
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(18, 4))
for ax, name in zip(axes, top4):
    cm = confusion_matrix(y_test, results[name]["preds"])
    sns.heatmap(cm, annot=True, fmt="d", cmap="Blues", ax=ax, cbar=False,
                xticklabels=["Fake","Real"], yticklabels=["Fake","Real"])
    ax.set_title(f"{name}\nAcc={results[name]['accuracy']:.4f}", fontsize=9)
    ax.set_xlabel("Predicted"); ax.set_ylabel("True")
plt.suptitle("Confusion Matrices — Top 4 Models", fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

7.6 Precision-Recall Curves¶

In [30]:
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 6))
for name, res in results.items():
    clf_pr = res["clf"]
    Xte_cur = res["Xte"]
    try:
        if hasattr(clf_pr, "predict_proba"):
            proba = clf_pr.predict_proba(Xte_cur)[:,1]
        else:
            continue
        precision_vals, recall_vals, _ = precision_recall_curve(y_test, proba)
        ap = average_precision_score(y_test, proba)
        ax.plot(recall_vals, precision_vals,
                label=f"{name[:20]} (AP={ap:.3f})", linewidth=1.2)
    except:
        pass
ax.set_xlabel("Recall"); ax.set_ylabel("Precision")
ax.set_title("Precision-Recall Curves", fontweight="bold")
ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper right")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

7.7 Cross-Validation (5-Fold Stratified)¶

In [31]:
cv = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=RANDOM_STATE)
top3_cv = res_df.head(3).index.tolist()
cv_results = {}
print("5-Fold Stratified Cross-Validation (top 3 models):")
for name in top3_cv:
    clf_cv = results[name]["clf"]
    Xtr_cv = results[name]["Xtr"]
    try:
        scores = cross_val_score(clf_cv, Xtr_cv, y_train, cv=cv,
                                  scoring="f1_macro", n_jobs=-1)
        cv_results[name] = scores
        print(f"  {name:<35} mean={scores.mean():.4f}  std={scores.std():.4f}  "
              f"{list(np.round(scores, 4))}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  {name:<35} ERROR: {e}")

7.9 Feature Importance — Logistic Regression Coefficients¶

In [33]:
lr_res = results.get("Logistic Regression") or results.get("Linear SVC")
if lr_res:
    clf_fi = lr_res["clf"]
    raw_clf = (clf_fi.calibrated_classifiers_[0].estimator
               if isinstance(clf_fi, CalibratedClassifierCV) else clf_fi)
    if hasattr(raw_clf, "coef_"):
        fn   = np.array(tfidf_word.get_feature_names_out())
        coef = raw_clf.coef_[0][:len(fn)]
        top_fake = np.argsort(coef)[:25]
        top_real = np.argsort(coef)[-25:][::-1]
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 7))
        for ax, idx, title, color in zip(axes,
                                          [top_fake, top_real],
                                          ["Top 25 → FAKE", "Top 25 → REAL"],
                                          [RED, BLUE]):
            ax.barh(fn[idx][::-1], np.abs(coef[idx])[::-1], color=color, alpha=0.85)
            ax.set_title(title, fontweight="bold")
            ax.set_xlabel("|Coefficient|")
        plt.suptitle("Logistic Regression – Most Influential TF-IDF Word Features",
                     fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
    else:
        print("Selected model has no coef_ attribute — skipping feature importance plot.")

STOP_WORDS   = set(stopwords.words('english'))
LEMMATIZER   = WordNetLemmatizer()
SIA          = SentimentIntensityAnalyzer()

def count_capitals(text): return sum(1 for c in text if c.isupper())
def exclamation_count(text): return text.count('!')
def question_count(text): return text.count('?')
def avg_word_len(text):
    words = text.split()
    return np.mean([len(w) for w in words]) if words else 0
def type_token_ratio(text):
    words = text.lower().split()
    return len(set(words)) / len(words) if words else 0
def count_quotes(text): return text.count('"') + text.count("'")
def has_url(text): return int(bool(re.search(r'http|www|\.com', text)))
def punct_ratio(text): return sum(1 for c in text if c in string.punctuation) / max(len(text), 1)
def sentence_count(text): return len(re.split(r'[.!?]+', text))
def avg_sentence_len(text):
    sents = [s.strip() for s in re.split(r'[.!?]+', text) if s.strip()]
    return np.mean([len(s.split()) for s in sents]) if sents else 0
def expand_contractions(text):
    for k, v in {"won't":'will not',"can't":'cannot',"n't":' not',
                 "'re":' are',"'ve":' have',"'ll":' will',
                 "'d":' would',"'m":' am',"it's":'it is'}.items():
        text = text.replace(k, v)
    return text
def clean_text(text, lemmatize=True, remove_stops=True):
    text = str(text).lower()
    text = expand_contractions(text)
    text = re.sub(r'http\S+|www\S+', ' URL ', text)
    text = re.sub(r'@\w+', ' USER ', text)
    text = re.sub(r'\d+', ' NUM ', text)
    text = re.sub(r'[^\w\s]', ' ', text)
    text = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text).strip()
    tokens = text.split()
    if remove_stops:
        tokens = [t for t in tokens if t not in STOP_WORDS and len(t) > 2]
    if lemmatize:
        tokens = [LEMMATIZER.lemmatize(t) for t in tokens]
    return ' '.join(tokens)

Section 8 — Dimensionality Reduction (LSA / SVD)¶

Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA) via Truncated SVD reduces the TF-IDF feature space from 60k dimensions to a dense, semantically meaningful lower-dimensional space.

In [36]:
svd200 = TruncatedSVD(n_components=200, random_state=RANDOM_STATE)
X_all_tfidf = tfidf_word.transform(df["clean"])
X_svd = svd200.fit_transform(X_all_tfidf)
print(f"Explained variance ratio (200 dims): {svd200.explained_variance_ratio_.sum():.4f}")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4))
cumvar = np.cumsum(svd200.explained_variance_ratio_)
ax.plot(range(1, 201), cumvar, color=BLUE, linewidth=1.5)
ax.axhline(0.5, color=RED, linestyle="--", label="50% variance")
ax.axhline(0.8, color="green", linestyle="--", label="80% variance")
ax.set_xlabel("Number of SVD Components")
ax.set_ylabel("Cumulative Explained Variance")
ax.set_title("LSA — Explained Variance Curve", fontweight="bold")
ax.legend(); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Section 9 — Unsupervised Learning & Clustering¶

We apply four clustering algorithms to SVD-100 reduced features and evaluate using internal metrics (silhouette, Davies-Bouldin) and external metrics (ARI, NMI).

In [38]:

y_all = df["label"].values

9.4 Agglomerative Clustering¶

In [41]:
samp_idx = np.random.RandomState(RANDOM_STATE).choice(len(X_svd100),
            size=min(5000, len(X_svd100)), replace=False)
X_samp = X_svd100[samp_idx]
y_samp = y_all[samp_idx]

agg = AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=2, linkage="ward")
agg_labels = agg.fit_predict(X_samp)
ari_agg = adjusted_rand_score(y_samp, agg_labels)

Section 10 — Topic Modeling¶

We apply LDA, NMF, and LSA to uncover latent thematic structure in the corpus.

In [45]:
cv_tm = CountVectorizer(max_features=25000, stop_words="english",
                         min_df=5, max_df=0.9)
X_cv_tm = cv_tm.fit_transform(df["clean"])
cv_fn = np.array(cv_tm.get_feature_names_out())

tfidf_tm = TfidfVectorizer(max_features=25000, stop_words="english",
                            min_df=5, max_df=0.9, sublinear_tf=True)
X_tf_tm = tfidf_tm.fit_transform(df["clean"])
tf_fn = np.array(tfidf_tm.get_feature_names_out())

TOP_W = 12

Section 11 — 2D Embeddings (t-SNE / UMAP)¶

We project SVD-100 features to 2D for visual inspection. Three views: true labels, KMeans clusters, dominant LDA topic.

In [51]:

y_viz = y_all[viz_idx]
km_viz = km_labels[viz_idx]

# t-SNE

            init="pca", random_state=RANDOM_STATE, n_jobs=-1)
X_tsne = tsne.fit_transform(X_viz)

# ── FIX: define scatter2d AND draw ALL subplots in the same cell ─────────────
n_plots = 3 + int(HAS_UMAP)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, n_plots, figsize=(6*n_plots, 5))

def scatter2d(ax, coords, colors, title, cmap="coolwarm"):
    sc = ax.scatter(coords[:,0], coords[:,1], c=colors, cmap=cmap,
                    alpha=0.4, s=6, rasterized=True)
    ax.set_title(title, fontweight="bold"); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
    plt.colorbar(sc, ax=ax, shrink=0.8)

scatter2d(axes[0], X_tsne, y_viz,  "t-SNE — True Labels (0=Fake,1=Real)")
scatter2d(axes[1], X_tsne, km_viz, "t-SNE — KMeans Clusters")

# LDA dominant topic
dom_lda = X_lda[viz_idx].argmax(axis=1)
scatter2d(axes[2], X_tsne, dom_lda, "t-SNE — Dominant LDA Topic", "tab10")

if HAS_UMAP:
    import umap as umap_lib
    reducer = umap_lib.UMAP(n_components=2, random_state=RANDOM_STATE, n_neighbors=30)
    X_umap = reducer.fit_transform(X_viz)
    scatter2d(axes[3], X_umap, y_viz, "UMAP — True Labels")

Section 12 — Anomaly Detection¶

We train an Isolation Forest exclusively on real news articles and treat articles that deviate from the real-news distribution as anomalies (potential fake).

In [52]:
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest

real_idx_pos = [i for i, l in enumerate(y_all) if l == 1]
fake_idx_pos = [i for i, l in enumerate(y_all) if l == 0]
X_real = X_svd100[real_idx_pos]
X_fake = X_svd100[fake_idx_pos]
In [53]:
iso = IsolationForest(n_estimators=100, contamination=0.1,
                       random_state=RANDOM_STATE, n_jobs=-1)
iso.fit(X_real)
scores_real = iso.decision_function(X_real)
scores_fake = iso.decision_function(X_fake)
print(f"Mean anomaly score – Real: {scores_real.mean():.4f}")
print(f"Mean anomaly score – Fake: {scores_fake.mean():.4f}")
print(f"(More negative = more anomalous)")

preds_iso_all = iso.predict(X_svd100)   # -1=anomaly, 1=inlier
pred_binary = (preds_iso_all == -1).astype(int)   # 1=predicted fake
ari_iso = adjusted_rand_score(y_all, pred_binary)
nmi_iso = normalized_mutual_info_score(y_all, pred_binary)
print(f"  ARI vs true labels: {ari_iso:.4f}  NMI: {nmi_iso:.4f}")

# Anomaly score distribution
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4))
ax.hist(scores_real, bins=50, alpha=0.6, color=BLUE, label="Real", density=True)
ax.hist(scores_fake, bins=50, alpha=0.6, color=RED,  label="Fake", density=True)
ax.axvline(0, color="black", linestyle="--", lw=1, label="Decision boundary")
ax.set_xlabel("Anomaly Score (higher = more normal)")
ax.set_title("Isolation Forest — Anomaly Score Distribution", fontweight="bold")
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Section 13 — Hyperparameter Tuning (GridSearchCV)¶

We tune the regularization strength C of Logistic Regression using 3-fold CV, optimizing for macro F1 score.

gs = GridSearchCV(lr_grid, param_grid, cv=3, scoring="f1_macro",
                   n_jobs=-1, verbose=0)
gs.fit(Xtr_tfidf, y_train)

gs_rep = classification_report(y_test, gs_preds, output_dict=True, zero_division=0)

14.2 Interactive Fake News Detector¶

The cell below builds a prediction function that:

  1. Preprocesses input title + text through the full pipeline
  2. Uses the best single model for a prediction
  3. Runs an ensemble vote across all trained models
  4. Displays a summary of linguistic features
In [56]:
best_pipe_clf = results[best_name]["clf"]

def preprocess_input(title, text):
    raw = title + " " + text
    cleaned = clean_text(raw)
    return raw, cleaned

def compute_features(raw, cleaned):
    sia_scores = SIA.polarity_scores(raw[:512])
    return {
        "word_count":    len(raw.split()),
        "cap_ratio":     count_capitals(raw) / max(len(raw), 1),
        "exclamation":   exclamation_count(raw),
        "question":      question_count(raw),
        "ttr":           type_token_ratio(raw),
        "avg_word_len":  avg_word_len(raw),
        "punct_ratio":   punct_ratio(raw),
        "compound":      sia_scores["compound"],
        "pos":           sia_scores["pos"],
        "neg":           sia_scores["neg"],
    }

def predict_article(title, text):
    raw, cleaned = preprocess_input(title, text)
    feat_dict = compute_features(raw, cleaned)

    # Build feature vector
    tfidf_vec = tfidf_word.transform([cleaned])
    char_vec  = tfidf_char.transform([cleaned])
    from scipy.sparse import csr_matrix, hstack as sp_hstack
    import pandas as pd
    hc_df = pd.DataFrame([feat_dict])[
        [k for k in HANDCRAFTED if k in feat_dict]].fillna(0)
    # Pad if needed
    for col in HANDCRAFTED:
        if col not in hc_df.columns:
            hc_df[col] = 0.0
    hc_df = hc_df[HANDCRAFTED]
    hc_vec = csr_matrix(scaler.transform(hc_df))
    combo  = sp_hstack([tfidf_vec, char_vec, hc_vec])

    pred = best_pipe_clf.predict(combo)[0]
    label_str = "REAL" if pred == 1 else "FAKE"
    try:
        score = best_pipe_clf.decision_function(combo)[0]
        score_str = f"{score:.3f}"
    except:
        score_str = "N/A"

    # Ensemble vote
    votes = {"FAKE": 0, "REAL": 0}
    for name, res in results.items():
        clf_e = res["clf"]
        Xte_type = res["Xte"]
        try:
            if Xte_type.shape[1] == Xtr_svd_trees.shape[1]:
                svd_vec = _svd_trees.transform(tfidf_vec)
                p = clf_e.predict(svd_vec)[0]
            elif Xte_type.shape[1] == Xtr_tfidf.shape[1]:
                p = clf_e.predict(tfidf_vec)[0]
            else:
                p = clf_e.predict(combo)[0]
            votes["REAL" if p == 1 else "FAKE"] += 1
        except:
            pass

    total_votes = sum(votes.values())
    print(f"\n{'─'*60}")
    print(f"TITLE: {title}")
    print(f"\nBest model ({best_name}): {label_str}  (score={score_str})")
    print(f"Ensemble vote: FAKE={votes['FAKE']}/{total_votes}  REAL={votes['REAL']}/{total_votes}")
    print(f"\nLinguistic features:")
    for k, v in feat_dict.items():
        print(f"  {k:<20}: {v:.4f}" if isinstance(v, float) else f"  {k:<20}: {v}")
    return label_str

# ── Demo ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("\n" + "="*60)
print("  FAKE NEWS DETECTOR — AUTO DEMO")
print("="*60)

predict_article(
    "BREAKING: Scientists Confirm Moon Made of Cheese",
    "Researchers at a top university have confirmed that the moon is entirely composed "
    "of aged cheddar. The shocking discovery overturns decades of space science!!!")

predict_article(
    "Federal Reserve raises interest rates by 0.25 percentage points",
    "The Federal Reserve on Wednesday raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter "
    "of a percentage point, as policymakers continue to battle persistent inflation "
    "while trying to avoid pushing the economy into recession.")
